questions.text: How long have you been noticing rectal bleeding, and how would you describe the colour — bright red, dark red, or mixed with stool?
questions.purpose: Characterise duration and character; dark blood mixed with stool is more concerning for proximal malignancy than bright red blood on toilet paper
options: Bright red, on toilet paper only, less than 4 weeks
Bright red, dripping into pan, less than 4 weeks
Dark red or mixed with stool, any duration

questions.text: Have you noticed a persistent change in bowel habit — such as looser stools, increased frequency, or alternating constipation and diarrhoea — lasting more than 4 weeks?
questions.purpose: Persistent bowel habit change with rectal bleeding is a key combined red flag for colorectal cancer

questions.text: Have you had significant unintentional weight loss or persistent fatigue alongside the rectal bleeding?
questions.purpose: Weight loss with rectal bleeding markedly increases colorectal cancer probability

questions.text: Are you aged 50 or over, or do you have a family history of colorectal cancer or bowel polyps?
questions.purpose: Age and family history are major risk factors for colorectal malignancy

questions.text: Do you have a sensation of incomplete bowel emptying (tenesmus) or feeling that your bowel never fully empties?
questions.purpose: Tenesmus can indicate a rectal mass obstructing complete emptying

questions.text: Do you have known haemorrhoids, anal fissure, or inflammatory bowel disease that could explain the bleeding?
questions.purpose: Identify common benign causes — but note these do not rule out concurrent malignancy in high-risk patients

questions.text: Have you had a previous colonoscopy or bowel cancer screening, and if so, when was it last performed?
questions.purpose: Establish screening history to guide urgency of investigation
options: Colonoscopy within last 3 years — polyps found
Positive stool screening test, no follow-up colonoscopy

questions.text: Have you noticed any abdominal mass, pain, or bloating alongside the rectal bleeding?
questions.purpose: Abdominal mass with rectal bleeding is a red flag for advanced colorectal malignancy
